questions.q: What is a Microsoft Sentinel Scheduled Analytics Rule?
options: A rule that runs a KQL query on a timer and generates an alert when the result count crosses a threshold
A rule that only runs once, manually, when an analyst clicks a button
A dashboard widget with no connection to any query
A setting that controls how long logs are retained in the workspace
questions.explain: A scheduled rule re-runs its KQL query on a timer and compares the result count against an alert threshold.

questions.q: Which setting controls how often a scheduled rule's query actually executes?
options: Run query every
Alert threshold
Entity mapping
Lookup data from the last
questions.explain: Run query every sets the execution frequency; the minimum is every 5 minutes.

questions.q: What does the "Lookup data from the last" setting control?
options: How far back in time each scheduled run scans when it executes the query
How many analysts can view the resulting incident
Which data connector the rule is allowed to use
The severity label applied to generated alerts
questions.explain: The lookback window defines how far back from "now" each run scans the data.

questions.q: Why does Microsoft recommend setting the lookback window longer than the run frequency?
options: Log ingestion isn't instantaneous, so a shorter or equal lookback can leave a gap where an event is never evaluated by any run
A longer lookback window is required by Azure billing rules
It has no real effect; the two settings are unrelated
Shorter lookback windows are not supported by the platform at all
questions.explain: A lookback window longer than the run frequency, often double, absorbs normal ingestion delay so events aren't missed.

questions.q: In this lesson's framing, what is a Scheduled Analytics Rule relative to the correlation rule concept taught earlier in this path?
options: It's the real, Sentinel-specific implementation of the same source / grouping key / threshold / action shape, now written in KQL with scheduling settings
It's an entirely unrelated feature with no connection to correlation rules
It replaces the need for any grouping key or threshold
It only applies to Microsoft's built-in security products, never to custom logic
questions.explain: The vendor-neutral correlation rule pseudocode maps directly onto a scheduled rule's query, schedule, threshold, and alert action.
